introduction.text: Klim Churyumov found this comet in 1969. Its two lobes meet at a narrow neck lined with steep cliffs.

model.title: Nucleus shape reconstruction
model.summary: Nucleus shape measured by Rosetta, simplified for display.

osiris.title: OSIRIS image mosaic
osiris.summary: Eight Rosetta photographs of cliffs, pits and smoother plains on both lobes, with original shadows and some seams.

albedo.title: VIRTIS single-scattering albedo
albedo.summary: How strongly surface grains scatter green light; higher values scatter more.

slope.title: VIRTIS visible spectral slope
slope.summary: How much reflectance rises from green to red light; higher values are redder.

absorption.title: VIRTIS 3.2 µm absorption depth
absorption.summary: Depth of the broad 3.2 µm absorption band. On its own, it does not show how much organic material is present.

ice.title: VIRTIS surface ice fraction
ice.summary: Estimated ice seen in reflected light, not ice inside the comet. Zero means the model fitted no ice.

regions.title: Named regions of 67P
regions.summary: Color separates the 26 named regions of the surface. They are geographic divisions, not minerals.

geology.title: Geological features mapped from OSIRIS
geology.summary: Fractures, cliffs, terraces and small features mapped from Rosetta images, drawn as symbols.
